title: 6. Key Features of the Indian Constitution (RRB Focus)

blocks.content:
• Written Constitution
• Federal System with Unitary Bias
• Parliamentary Form of Government
• Independent Judiciary
• Secular State
• Universal Adult Franchise
• Single Citizenship
India is often described as a “Union of States.”

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Indian Constitution features a Federal System with Unitary Bias, an Integrated Judiciary, and Single Citizenship.
The Preamble represents the heart of the Constitution, reflecting its underlying philosophy and key objectives.
India is defined as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.
The terms 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were incorporated into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
In the Indian Republic, the Head of State is elected rather than hereditary.

blocks.content:
The Preamble reflects the philosophy and objectives of the Constitution.
India is described as:
• Sovereign – India is internally and externally independent.
• Socialist – Wealth should be distributed to reduce inequality.
• Secular – Equal respect for all religions.
• Democratic – Government elected by the people.

• Republic – Head of State is elected, not hereditary.
IMPORTANT: Words *Socialist* and *Secular* were added by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**.
